18:         self.verbose = verbose
19:         hg_commits = set(hg_commits)
20:         hg_commits.update(commit[:12] for commit in list(hg_commits))
21:         self.hg_commits = frozenset(hg_commits)

23:     def successful_response(self, response, url):
24:         content_type = 'text/plain'
25:         headers = [("Content-Type", 'text/plain'),
26:                    ("Location", url)]
27:         response("303 See Other", headers)
28:         return []

34:                 '/lookup/rSVNREVISION\n']

1: PSF Infrastructure Overview
2: ===========================
3: 
4: The PSF runs a wide variety of infrastructure services to support its mission
5: from the `PyCon site <https://us.pycon.org>`_ to the `CPython Mercurial server
6: <https://hg.python.org>`_. The goal of this page is to enumerate all these
7: services, where they run, and who the main contact points are.
8: 
9: The Infrastructure Team
10: -----------------------
11: 
12: The infrastructure team is ultimately responsible for maintaining PSF
13: infrastructure. It is not, however, required to be a member of the
14: infrastructure to run a PSF service. Indeed, the day to day operations of most
15: services are handled by people not on the infrastructure team. The
16: infrastructure team can assist in setting up new services and advise maintainers
17: of individual services. Its members also generally handle changes to sensitive
18: global systems such as DNS. The currrent team members are:
19: 
20: * Alex Gaynor (has no responsibilities)
21: * Benjamin Peterson
22: * Benjamin W. Smith
23: * Donald Stufft
24: * Ernest W. Durbin III (PSF Director of Infrastructure)
25: * Noah Kantrowitz
26: 
27: The best way to contact the infrastructure team is mailing
28: infrastructure-staff@python.org. There's also often people hanging out on the
29: #python-infra channel of `Freenode <http://freenode.net>`_.
30: 
31: Infrastructure Providers
32: ------------------------
33: 
34: The PSF uses several different cloud providers and services for its infrastructure.
35: 
36: XS4ALL
37:    XS4ALL is the by far the oldest Python infrastructure provider. There are two
38:    physical servers owned by the PSF at XS4ALL: albatross and dinsdale. (There
39:    also used to be one called ximinez, but it seems to be unreachable now.)
40:    albatross is the mail server. dinsdale hosts a number of legacy services. We
41:    try not to put anything new on the XS4ALL servers, preferring modern cloud
42:    providers.
43: 
44: OSUOSL
45:    `Oregon State University Open Source Lab <http://osuosl.org/>`_ hosts VMs for
46:    the PSF. These VMs are provisioned using `Chef <http://www.getchef.com>`_ and
47:    their configuration management is in the `psf-chef git repo
48:    <https://github.com/python/psf-chef>`_.
49: 
50: Rackspace
51:    `Rackspace <http://www.rackspace.com>`_ was the primary cloud provider
52:    utilized by the PSF until March 2019.  `Salt <http://www.saltstack.com>`_
53:    is used for configuration management.
54: 
55: Dyn & Gandi
56:    `Gandi <http://www.gandi.net>`_ is our domain registar, and we use `Dyn
57:    <http://www.dyn.com>`_ for DNS hosting on most of our domains.
58: 
59: Pingdom
60:   `Pingdom <https://www.pingdom.com>`_ provides monitoring and complains to us
61:   when services are down.
62: 
63: Fastly
64:    `Fastly <http://www.fastly.com>`_ generously donates its content distribution
65:    network (CDN) to the PSF. Our highest traffic services (i.e. PyPI,
66:    www.python.org, docs.python.org) use this CDN to improve end-user latency.
67: 
68: Heroku
69:    `Heroku <https://heroku.com>`_ hosts many of the CPython core workflow bots,
70:    ephemeral or proof of concept apps, as well as other web apps that are well
71:    suited to it's platform.
72: 
73: DigitalOcean
74:    `DigitalOcean <https://digitalocean.com>`_ is the current target for most of
75:    the infrastructure we currently host in Rackspace, services deployed here
76:    are managed by `Salt <http://www.saltstack.com>`_.
77: 
78: 
79: Datacenters
80: -----------
81: 
82: ====== ============= ======
83: PSF DC Provider      Region
84: ====== ============= ======
85: iad1   Rackspace     IAD
86: ord1   Rackspace     ORD
87: ams1   Digital Ocean AMS3
88: nyc1   Digital Ocean NYC3
89: sfo1   Digital Ocean SFO2
90: ====== ============= ======
91: 
92: 
93: Details of Various Services
94: ---------------------------
95: 
96: This section enumerates PSF services, generalities about their hosting, and contact information for the owners.
97: 
98: Buildbot
99:    The `buildbot master <http://buildbot.python.org>`_ is a service run by
100:    python-dev@python.org, particularly Antoine Pitrou and Zach Ware.
101: 
102: bugs.python.org
103:    bugs.python.org is hosted by the PSF on DigitalOcean, powered by Roundup.
104:    It also hosts bugs.jython.org and issues.roundup-tracker.org. 
105: 
106: docs.python.org
107:    The Python documentation is hosted on DigitalOcean, served through Fastly,
108:    and owned by Julien Palard.
109: 
110: hg.python.org
111:    The CPython Mercurial repositories are hosted on a Rackspace VM. The service
112:    is owned by Antoine Pitrou and Georg Brandl.
113: 
114: mail.python.org
115:    The python.org `Mailman <http://list.org>`_ instance is hosted on
116:    https://mail.python.org as well as SMTP (Postfix). All inquiries should be
117:    directed to postmaster@python.org.
118: 
119: planetpython.org and planet.jython.org
120:    These are hosted on a Rackspace VM. The Planet code and configuration are
121:    `hosted on GitHub <https://github.com/python/planet>`_ and maintained by the
122:    team at planet@python.org.
123: 
124: pythontest.net
125:    `pythontest.net <www.pythontest.net>`_ hosts services and files used by the
126:    Python test suite. python-dev@python.org is ultimately responsible for its
127:    maintenance.
128: 
129: speed.python.org
130:    speed.python.org is a `Codespeed <https://github.com/tobami/codespeed>`_
131:    `instance <https://github.com/zware/codespeed>`_ tracking Python performance.
132:    The web interface is hosted on a Rackspace VM, benchmarks are run on a beefy
133:    machine at OSUOSL and scheduled by the Buildbot master.  Maintained by
134:    speed@python.org and Zach Ware.
135: 
136: wiki.python.org
137:    This is hosted on an OSUOSL VM. Marc-André Lemburg owns it.
138: 
139: www.jython.org
140:    This is hosted on a Rackspace VM. The setup is quite simple and shouldn't

142: 
143: www.python.org
144:    The `main Python website <https://www.python.org>`_ is a Django app hosted on

151:    https://staging.python.org for testing the site. http://legacy.python.org is
152:    the old website hosted on dinsdale.
153: 
154: PyCon
155:    The PyCon website is hosted on Heroku. The contact address is
156:    pycon-tech@python.org.
157: 
158: PyPI
159:    The `Python Package Index <https://pypi.org/>`_ sees the most load of
160:    any PSF service. Its source code is available `on GitHub
161:    <https://github.com/pypa/warehouse>`_. All of its infrastructure runs on
162:    AWS configured by `pypi-salt <https://github.com/python/pypi-salt>`_,
163:    and it is served over Fastly. The infrastructure is maintained by Ernest

165:    admin@mail.pypi.org.
166: 
167: PyPy properties
168:    The `PyPy website <http://pypy.org>`_ is hosted on a OSUOSL VM and maintained
169:    by pypy-dev@python.org.
